stimulus_db: Hospital patients generally have lower infection rates and require shorter hospital stays if they are housed in private rooms rather than semiprivate rooms. Yet in Woodville's hospital, which has only semiprivate rooms, infection rates and length of stays are typically the same as in several nearby hospitals where most of the rooms are private, even though patients served by these hospitals are very similar to those served by Woodville's hospital.
stem_db: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent conflict in the information above?

choices_db.A: Many of the doctors who routinely treat patients in Woodville's hospital also routinely treat patients in one or more of the nearby hospitals.
choices_db.B: Most of the nearby hospitals were built within the last 10 years, whereas Woodville's hospital was built about 50 years ago.
choices_db.C: Infection is more likely to be spread where people come into close contact with one another than where they do not.
choices_db.D: Woodville's hospital has a policy of housing one patient per room in semiprivate rooms whenever possible.
choices_db.E: Woodville's hospital is located in its central business district, whereas most of the nearby hospitals are located outside their municipalities' business districts.

steps.label: Given that
steps.body: Patients in private rooms generally get fewer infections and shorter stays than patients in semiprivate rooms.

steps.label: How can it be that
steps.body: Woodville's hospital has only semiprivate rooms, yet its infection rates and stays match nearby hospitals with mostly private rooms and very similar patients?

steps.label: Evaluate
steps.body: The patients are similar, so look at how the rooms are used. A semiprivate room is built for two, but if Woodville often puts only one patient in it, its patients get the benefit of a private room.

steps.label: Goal
steps.body: Find a difference between Woodville and the nearby hospitals that gives Woodville's patients the benefits of private rooms.

notes.body: We want a distinction between Woodville and nearby hospitals, and this provides a similarity.
We want a reason why Woodville is doing better than we'd expect, and being told that it is an older hospital seems more to be a reason why it would do worse than one might expect.

This is reinforcing the background claim, explaining why private rooms tend to lead to lower infection rates and shorter hospital stays.
It does nothing to explain the surprise, which is why Woodville's semiprivate rooms seem to be doing as well as other hospitals' private rooms.

We want a reason Woodville's semiprivate rooms do as well as other hospitals' private rooms, and this gives it.

If Woodville puts one patient in each semiprivate room whenever it can, then in practice most of its patients get a room to themselves. So Woodville gets the benefits of private rooms without having any, and the surprise goes away.

For this to explain the surprise, we'd have to think that being located in the central business district has some common sense connection to lower infection rates or shorter hospital stays, which would definitely be walking on thin ice.
